name: zana-community
description: Public plugins contributed by the Zana community.

plugins.description: Pin browser elements, write precise feedback, and attach captured element context to your Zana thread composer.
plugins.overview:
Annotate a web page beside a Zana thread. Choose Annotate elements in the browser toolbar, click an element, and save your feedback. Numbered pins attach the element text, selector, styles, and best-effort React component context as compact composer references.

Edit or remove pins before sending. Successful send or queue clears the pins; sent messages retain immutable snapshots. The plugin adds no sidebar item.

Requires Zana desktop with the browser annotation support merged in salesforce/zana PR #622, including experimental_browserToolbarAction and the scoped page bridge. Upgrade older builds before installing. No separate browser automation service, CLI, account, or API key is required.

Installed plugins run as full-trust code in the Zana server process. This plugin inspects the page you annotate and stores captured context locally; that context is shared with your selected agent provider when you send the thread message.

An MIT-licensed port of BB Agent Annotations by Michael Yong, retaining the original overlay, capture implementation, and license notice.

plugins.description: Run Zana threads through Google’s Antigravity Native ACP server, with account controls, native models, planning and subscription usage.
plugins.overview:
Add Google Antigravity as a Zana thread provider through the Native ACP server, agy_acp_server. Use the native model catalogue, Plan mode, account recovery from the thread side panel, and subscription usage checks in Settings.

## Get started

Install with `zcc marketplace install provider-antigravity@zana-community`. Open Settings → Antigravity Provider, choose your authentication method, and verify the session and models. Start a thread and select Antigravity.

## Requirements

Requires a compatible Zana desktop build (the package declares Zana >=2.2.2), network access, and a Google account or credentials entitled to use the selected authentication method and models. Google subscription or API charges apply separately. Model availability depends on your account. Supported runtime targets are macOS Apple Silicon and Intel, Linux x64 and arm64, and Windows x64.

## Runtime and credentials

The plugin can download a managed Google Native ACP distribution and verifies its archive with SHA-256 before extraction. You can configure a native executable override. It supports personal OAuth, business OAuth, Gemini API key and agent-platform authentication. Credentials and settings are maintained locally; thread content is sent to the selected Google service.

## Distribution

Maintained by Ros Haitovich in matrostik/zana-plugins. This listing pins version 0.3.0’s source commit, including compiled server, UI and host artifacts. Installed plugins run as full-trust code in Zana’s server process.

plugins.description: AI pull request reviews for GitHub and GitHub Enterprise on Zana's providers: review inbox, multi-model consensus, risk and quality scores, Deep Review threads, and posting findings.
plugins.overview:
Triage and AI-review GitHub pull requests in Zana using the AI providers you already configured.

## What you get

- **Review Inbox**: A dedicated sidebar inbox with three lists — Needs my review, Mine, and Watched — showing CI state and latest review status for each pull request. Supports GitHub and GitHub Enterprise hosts simultaneously.
- **Multi-Model Consensus**: Run automated PR reviews across multiple AI models configured in Zana. Consensus findings agreed upon by multiple models are merged and ranked higher.
- **Scores and Findings**: Comprehensive risk, test coverage, requirements, simplicity, and stability scores, alongside security, performance, logic, and style findings.
- **Requirements Extraction**: Automatically derives review criteria from PR title, description, linked GitHub issues, and repository spec files.
- **Interactive Findings Workflow**: Filter by severity and category, inspect collapsible file groups with highlighted context, edit findings, or dismiss with undo/restore.
- **Post to GitHub**: Publish selected findings directly as GitHub PR review comments with sign-off confirmation.
- **Local Reviews**: Review uncommitted, staged, or branch changes on local checkouts before opening a PR, capturing an immutable snapshot commit.
- **Deep Review**: Spawn dedicated Zana threads with full PR context for interactive exploration.
- **CLI & Agent Tools**: `zcc codewink` terminal CLI and agent tools (`codewink_list_prs`, `codewink_get_review`, `codewink_review_pr`, `codewink_review_local`).

## Get started

Install with `zcc marketplace install codewink@zana-community`. Configure your GitHub host and token in Settings → CodeWink or authenticate via `gh auth login`.

## Requirements

Requires Zana >=1.0.0 and one or more configured AI providers. GitHub authentication supports GitHub CLI (`gh`), Git credential helper, or personal access tokens.

## Distribution

Maintained by Ros Haitovich in matrostik/zana-plugins. Pinned to commit 391700c9479a97ed17561270a7b18e090d7a5b03 (v0.2.2). Installed plugins run as full-trust code in Zana's server process.

plugins.description: Let Zana agents see and operate macOS and Windows apps with Cua Driver, one-thread desktop control and approval prompts for sensitive actions.
plugins.overview:
Let agents inspect native app windows, take screenshots, click and type through Cua Driver on the computer running Zana. One thread holds the desktop lease at a time, and it is released when the turn finishes, fails or closes. Sensitive actions such as foreground input, whole-desktop access, clipboard use, file uploads and force-quit ask for approval by default.

Includes Cua Driver 0.33.4 for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, and Windows x64 and ARM64. Open Plugins → Computer Use → Configuration to prepare the included driver locally or select an existing installation. The Git package includes compiled runtime files and about 135 MB of driver archives; no separate dependency installation or build is needed. Included-driver setup works offline.

Requires Zana desktop on macOS or Windows, an unlocked interactive desktop, and the required OS permissions. macOS requires Accessibility and Screen Recording permission for the selected CuaDriver.app; Windows requires the same interactive user session and may refuse elevated apps or UAC prompts. Opening Zana remotely controls the desktop of its host machine. CLI-agent sessions do not receive the plugin tools.

Adds agent tools, a setup guide, desktop status and lease controls, a thread Desktop tab and the zcc cua-driver CLI. It does not add a sidebar entry. The daemon uses standard or bounded permissions, and the plugin refuses a daemon running in unrestricted mode. Leases and approval prompts apply to calls through this plugin. Cua Driver has upstream telemetry on by default; Configuration shows its state and can disable it.

Installed plugins run as full-trust code in the Zana server process. Native macOS setup and configuration have recorded live verification. Windows behavior is covered by fake-driver tests; no Windows live verification is claimed. The optional agent cursor currently covers only the main monitor on macOS.

plugins.description: Connect Orgo Linux computers to Zana with automatic SSH setup, and manage their power state from one panel.
plugins.overview:
Connect a running Orgo Linux computer to Zana from the sidebar. The plugin prepares a dedicated SSH key, updates its managed SSH configuration, and pairs the machine through Zana. Reconnect refreshes changed endpoints and reuses existing enrollments.

Browse computers across Orgo workspaces, filter the list, inspect SSH details, and start, stop, restart, suspend or resume computers when supported. Destructive power actions ask for confirmation.

Requires Zana desktop on macOS or Linux, an Orgo account with API access, and a running Linux Orgo computer for pairing. Orgo subscription and usage charges apply separately. Configure the API key in the private local credential file described in the repository README.

Installed plugins execute as full-trust code in the Zana server process. This plugin contacts Orgo over HTTPS and writes its dedicated SSH identity and managed configuration locally. It preserves existing SSH keys and does not receive host-daemon tokens.

plugins.description: Independent Salesforce workbench and Agentforce Studio: connected orgs, SOQL, Apex, deployments and agent tools. Install with `zcc plugin install salesforce@official`.
plugins.overview:
Salesforce DX inner loop for ZCC: org identity, SOQL, Apex, LWC, and Agentforce tools with fail-closed mutation confirms.

## What you get

- Org identity and doctor checks for the connected Salesforce org.
- SOQL Explorer, Apex and LWC editors, and Agentforce playground and preview.
- Agent tools that require an explicit confirm before any mutating API call.

## How it works

The plugin talks to Salesforce APIs from this host. Reads can run unattended. Writes wait for your approval in the thread.

## Requirements

Install with `zcc plugin install salesforce@official`, then authenticate the Salesforce CLI / DX org this project uses.

## Independent distribution

Maintained in grebmann1/zcc-plugin-salesforce with its own compiled releases. Salesforce is optional on new Zana installations. Existing installations migrate with their settings, saved data and enablement preserved.

plugins.description: Hear Orc, Human and Murloc voices when an agent needs input or becomes idle. Mix characters per alert and download only the voices you want.
plugins.overview:
Give your agents Warcraft voices: Orc Peon, Human Peasant, Orc Grunt and Murloc. Choose a different character for Needs you and Becomes idle, or use one character for both. Preview each alert in a Warcraft-inspired interface.

Open Settings → Notifications → Sounds, select Warcraft Voices, download the characters you want and choose a voice for each alert. Enable Becomes idle if wanted, then turn on Play notification sounds. Installing the plugin does not change your active sound provider.

Quiet spacing, rotating clips, volume controls and a 30-minute pause help keep multiple sessions manageable. Input alerts take priority; idle means the agent is at rest, not that its work succeeded.

Automatic alerts and the Settings integration require a Zana desktop build containing salesforce/zana PR #698 and the notificationSoundProvider SDK slot. Older hosts retain downloads and manual previews in the plugin Configure section, with automatic playback off. The Git release includes compiled runtime files; no separate CLI, account, API key or dependency installation is needed. Internet access is needed to download characters.

Installed plugins run as full-trust code in the Zana server process. This plugin downloads requested audio from a pinned PeonPing/og-packs revision on GitHub, checks file signatures and SHA-256 hashes, and stores clips and preferences locally. It runs one selected sound provider across windows.

Plugin source code is MIT licensed. Game audio is not bundled. Upstream PeonPing pack manifests declare CC-BY-NC-4.0; source attribution and applicable audio rights are linked in the plugin and its README.
